biography.plain_text: Bernd Schottdorf was a German physician who built a major laboratory diagnostics business in Augsburg. He combined medical practice with the expansion of a nationwide laboratory network. His wife Gabriele led its daily operations, while he concentrated on business development. The group eventually became wholly owned by Australia's Sonic Healthcare.

long_biography.plain_text:
Laboratory entrepreneur Bernd Schottdorf also pursued a substantial career as a self-taught painter. Repeated journeys to Africa supplied subjects for his landscapes, portraits and scenes of markets and harbours. His work extended to photography, ceramics and sculpture; an exhibition at Wemding's KunstMuseum Donau-Ries brought his paintings and photographs into dialogue with the museum's African art collection.

His technical interests continued beyond medicine. Working with Carbon Terra, he explored the production of biochar from plant material. He filed a patent application for a continuously fed reactor that used internal heating rods to turn biomass into charcoal without oxygen. The patent proposed mixing biochar with compost to enrich agricultural soils.
